full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: This rule was issued, at the instance of the accused-petitioner, calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceeding of GR case No. 208 of 2005 arising out of Cox's Bazar PS. Case No. 20. dated 21-6-2005 under sections 143/385/448/427/323/354/380 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of learned Magistrate, 1St Class, Cognizance Court No. 1, Cox's Bazar should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. On 9-4-2005 one Golbahar Begum filed a petition in the Cognizance Court No. 1, Cox's Bazar implicating the accused-petitioner and others in the offence punishable under sections 143/385/448/427/323/354/380 of the Penal Code but the then learned Magistrate sent it to the local police station to treat it as FIR and ultimately a case was recorded, being Cox's Bazar PS Case No. 20 dated 21-6-2005. On investigation final report was submitted with a recommendation to discharge the accused-petitioner of the offence noted above. Thereafter a Naraji-Petition was filed which was again sent it to police authority to ensure for further investigation which was also ended in final report so far it relates to the accused-petitioner and also with a recommendation to stand trial of the other accused named in the FIR. Again a Naraji-Petition was filed which was handed over to the then learned Magistrate 1st Class for judicial inquiry who also submitted a report that implication of the accused-petitioner was not found; as such, he did not recommend the trial of the accused-petitioner.
